{
"subevents": [
{"id": "0", "subevent": "A new survey by Human Rights Watch found that the lives of LGBTQ+ people in Afghanistan have dramatically worsened under Taliban rule."},
{"id": "1", "subevent": "The report documented nearly 60 cases of targeted violence against LGBTQ+ people since August 2021."},
{"id": "2", "subevent": "Heather Barr of Human Rights Watch stated that before the Taliban takeover, LGBTQ+ people had hope for gradual improvement, but that ended on August 15."},
{"id": "3", "subevent": "The report noted that while homosexuality was already illegal under the previous government, the Taliban vowed to take a hard line against LGBT people, citing sharia law."},
{"id": "4", "subevent": "J Lester Feder of OutRight Action International reported cases of gang-rape, mob attacks, and family members hunting LGBT Afghans, with no hope of protection, and few options to flee."},
{"id": "5", "subevent": "A 16-year-old transgender girl, Zeba Gul, described being locked up, beaten, and abused by her family before and after the Taliban takeover."},
{"id": "6", "subevent": "After the Taliban came to power, Zeba Gul's family threw her out, and she was attacked, raped, and held and beaten by the Taliban."},
{"id": "7", "subevent": "Faraydoon Fakoori of Paiwand 34 stated that the situation has worsened for gender minorities with increased violence, harassment, and rape."},
{"id": "8", "subevent": "Zeba Gul commented that the Taliban's return empowered vigilantes and homophobes, making it open season on LGBT people with no fear of punishment."},
{"id": "9", "subevent": "In 2021, a Taliban spokesperson stated that homosexuals face stoning or being crushed by a wall."}
]
}

{
  "subevents": [
    {"id": "0", "subevent": "Social workers and mental health experts in Fiji called for more tender loving care to address the mental health crisis, especially targeting vulnerable populations during the Covid-19 pandemic."},
    {"id": "1", "subevent": "Lifeline Fiji released suicide statistics for January to July 2021 showing 47 suicides and 65 attempted suicides."},
    {"id": "2", "subevent": "Fiji's Health Ministry recorded 72 suicides in 2020, down from 89 in the same period in 2019."},
    {"id": "3", "subevent": "Fiji Council of Social Services director Vani Catanasiga urged that suicide data from different agencies be made available centrally to enable a more strategic response, and said mental health support needs to be increased."},
    {"id": "4", "subevent": "Mental health specialist Selina Kuruleca agreed, stating that the pandemic has turned into a mental health epidemic and pleaded with the government to listen to suffering people."},
    {"id": "5", "subevent": "Kuruleca said people need to be heard and reassured that the government cares, and that the government is responsible for the welfare of its people."},
    {"id": "6", "subevent": "Kuruleca noted that life in poverty-stricken communities had worsened during the pandemic, with many people living in crowded conditions and requiring more than just food assistance."},
    {"id": "7", "subevent": "On Tuesday, 118 new Covid-19 cases were reported in the community, and one death was confirmed: a 59-year-old man who died after 28 days in hospital."},
    {"id": "8", "subevent": "Health Secretary James Fong reported four additional deaths of Covid-positive patients classified due to pre-existing conditions, and gave current hospitalizations: 114 patients, with two severe and two critical."},
    {"id": "9", "subevent": "Dr. Fong reported 113 new recoveries, bringing active cases to 12,948, total cases to 50,198 since March 2020, and death toll to 576."}
  ]
}

{"subevents": [{"id": "0", "subevent": "Sri Lanka re-opened schools for primary students on Monday after almost five months."}, {"id": "1", "subevent": "The Education Ministry said students are permitted to attend school in suitable attire from Monday."}, {"id": "2", "subevent": "Education Secretary Professor Kapila Perera explained the decision was reached because many students could not source school material and uniforms given the present situation, and emphasized that attending school is most important."}, {"id": "3", "subevent": "Sri Lanka’s health sector called on education authorities and parents to ensure all necessary health guidelines are followed."}, {"id": "4", "subevent": "Director-General of Health Services Dr. Asela Gunawardena told News 1st that parents must refrain from sending their children to school if they are ill or have a fever."}]}

{"subevents": [{"id": "0", "subevent": "The United States announced 10% tariffs on European-made Airbus planes and 25% duties on French wine, Scotch and Irish whiskies, and cheese from across Europe as punishment for illegal EU aircraft subsidies."}, {"id": "1", "subevent": "The World Trade Organization authorized the United States to impose tariffs on $7.5 billion worth of EU goods annually in the long-running aircraft subsidies case."}, {"id": "2", "subevent": "The U.S. tariff list includes large Airbus planes made in France, Britain, Germany and Spain, but exempts EU-made aircraft parts used in Airbus' Alabama assembly operations and those used by Boeing."}, {"id": "3", "subevent": "U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer said the WTO confirmed the U.S. is entitled to impose countermeasures and that the U.S. expects to enter negotiations with the EU."}, {"id": "4", "subevent": "The tariffs target Spanish olives, British sweaters and woollens, German tools and coffee, British whisky, French wine, and cheese from nearly every EU country, but spare Italian wine and olive oil."}, {"id": "5", "subevent": "The size and scope of the tariffs were reduced from a $25 billion list floated earlier this year, and the USTR warned it can increase the tariffs at any time."}, {"id": "6", "subevent": "The USTR sought WTO ratification of its tariff list by Oct. 14, with duties possibly coming into force three days after a scheduled tariff increase on Chinese goods."}, {"id": "7", "subevent": "Airbus spokesman Clay McConnell said the company was evaluating the list and that the WTO would grant the EU authority to impose tariffs on U.S. goods over Boeing subsidies."}, {"id": "8", "subevent": "Delta Air Lines said it has about 170 Airbus planes on order that could be affected, warning that tariffs would inflict serious harm on U.S. airlines."}]}

{"subevents": [{"id": "0", "subevent": "Malaysia arrested more than 4,000 people for violating lockdown orders as it entered a harsher phase of its Movement Control Order, with police setting up roadblocks and arresting a man who jumped into the Strait of Malacca."}, {"id": "1", "subevent": "Senior Minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob announced the shift to harsh mode at a press conference, urging people to adhere to the order."}, {"id": "2", "subevent": "Lockdown enforcement varies globally, but Malaysia reports one of the highest arrest rates with 4,189 arrested since March 18 and 1,449 charged, while the Philippines arrested over 20,000 and President Duterte threatened to shoot violators."}, {"id": "3", "subevent": "Malaysia reported that the lockdown is decreasing the spread of COVID-19, with 3,116 total cases and 50 deaths as of Friday."}, {"id": "4", "subevent": "Google data showed an 81% decrease in Malaysian citizens' presence at retail and recreation sites compared to about a month earlier."}, {"id": "5", "subevent": "Authorities cracked down on speech by arresting people for alleged misinformation online, leading journalists to self-censor, and human rights advocates warned of curtailed free expression."}, {"id": "6", "subevent": "Political turmoil followed Mahathir Mohamad's failed attempt to consolidate power in February, leading to the old ruling party returning to power in March, which economists said will hinder the fight against the virus."}, {"id": "7", "subevent": "The government announced a $57.3 billion stimulus package called PRIHATIN to address the economic impact of COVID-19, as Malaysia is among the first economies in the region to predict a recession."}]}

{"subevents": [{"id": "0", "subevent": "Pope Francis appoints Sr. Alessandra Smerilli as interim Secretary of the Dicastery for Promoting Integral Human Development and as a delegate of the Vatican Covid-19 Commission."}, {"id": "1", "subevent": "Sr. Smerilli replaces Msgr. Bruno Marie Duffé and Fr. Augusto Zampini, who have returned to their dioceses."}, {"id": "2", "subevent": "Sr. Smerilli has served as Undersecretary at the Dicastery since March 2021."}, {"id": "3", "subevent": "Pope Francis orders that the management team of the Vatican Covid-19 Commission be composed of Cardinal Turkson, Sr. Smerilli, and Fr. Fabio Baggio."}, {"id": "4", "subevent": "Sr. Smerilli expresses gratitude for the appointment and commits to serve with humility, passion, and a spirit of obedience."}, {"id": "5", "subevent": "Fr. Augusto Zampini announces his return to his diocese and expresses confidence in Sr. Smerilli's leadership."}]}

{"subevents": [{"id": "0", "subevent": "President Obama announced new actions to reduce gun violence, including increased funding for mental health treatment and enhanced background checks."}, {"id": "1", "subevent": "Mental health advocates say media reports of mass shootings reinforce the impression that severe mental illness leads to violence, but studies show most people with severe mental illness are not violent."}, {"id": "2", "subevent": "People with serious mental illness account for about 4% of firearm homicides, while suicides constituted 61% of gun deaths in 2014."}, {"id": "3", "subevent": "Jeffrey Swanson says gun violence and mental illness have very little overlap and fixing the mental health system is not a silver bullet for reducing gun violence."}, {"id": "4", "subevent": "Mental health stakeholders are concerned about reinforcing the false association between mental illness and violence and call for criteria based on dangerous behavior rather than diagnosis alone."}, {"id": "5", "subevent": "Obama proposed a $500 million investment in mental health access, but some criticized including mental health reform in gun violence reduction orders."}, {"id": "6", "subevent": "Swanson supports comprehensive background checks with criteria based on risk indicators like violent assault convictions, restraining orders, and multiple DUIs, not just mental health history."}, {"id": "7", "subevent": "Studies found that a handgun ban in D.C. reduced gun suicides, Connecticut's permit-to-purchase law lowered gun suicide rates by 15%, and Missouri's repeal raised them by 16%."}, {"id": "8", "subevent": "Researchers monitor gun violence restraining orders, and Swanson notes that mass shooters like Jared Loughner and James Holmes had never been involuntarily committed and could legally purchase firearms."}]}

{"subevents": [{"id": "0", "subevent": "A new book reveals unprecedented details about Emperor Akihito's spending of public money and his royal staff."}, {"id": "1", "subevent": "The main imperial palace requires 160 servants, with rules like maids not allowed to both wipe a table and wipe the floor, and the monthly water bill is £50,000."}, {"id": "2", "subevent": "The book draws on about 200 documents made available for the first time under a new public information law, ending the 'Chrysanthemum Curtain' of secrecy."}, {"id": "3", "subevent": "Author Yohei Mori calls the disclosure an epochal step forward, but the Imperial Household Agency refused to answer follow-up questions promptly."}, {"id": "4", "subevent": "Details include a £2 million-a-year clinic with 28 daily visitors, a £140,000 room redecoration for Princess Aiko's birth, a 961-strong police force costing £48 million, and a £140,000 wine cellar storing expensive wines."}, {"id": "5", "subevent": "The imperial family consists of six inner court members and 19 others on the civil list, with Prince Tomohito's family receiving £310,000 a year despite light royal duties."}, {"id": "6", "subevent": "Mori says discussion has been stifled by secrecy and lack of scrutiny; the book reveals that imperial men outside the direct line of succession receive twice as much as their wives."}, {"id": "7", "subevent": "Princess Sayako has visited 12 countries since 1989; the imperial farm costs £3 million a year; much of the family's wealth was confiscated after World War II."}, {"id": "8", "subevent": "Some spending restraint exists: the emperor's entourage pays only £110 per night for hotels, which owners accept for the honor of hosting the imperial family."}]}

{"subevents": [{"id": "0", "subevent": "Deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon rose more than 50% in the first three months of 2020 compared to the same period in 2019."}, {"id": "1", "subevent": "Scientists warned that President Bolsonaro's development-friendly policies could push the Amazon past a tipping point, transforming it into a savannah-like state that emits more carbon than it absorbs."}, {"id": "2", "subevent": "Brazil's environmental agency scaled back enforcement measures during the COVID-19 pandemic, increasing the vulnerability of the forest and indigenous tribes."}, {"id": "3", "subevent": "Indigenous leaders reported ongoing invasions by loggers and hunters, and expressed fear that the virus could devastate isolated tribes."}, {"id": "4", "subevent": "Bolsonaro slashed funding at FUNAI and in April 2020, FUNAI passed law IN 09, preventing undemarcated indigenous lands from being labeled as indigenous in the land registry, which critics said aids illegal occupiers."}, {"id": "5", "subevent": "Provisional Measure MP 910, decreed in December 2019, is being considered for permanent law, allowing illegal occupiers of federal lands to purchase them at reduced prices, potentially leading to 16,000 square kilometers of deforestation by 2027; the administration denied it facilitates land-grabbing."}, {"id": "6", "subevent": "Since enforcement rollbacks, reports of illegal logging and violent attacks increased; in April, illegal gold mining rose in the Yanomami reserve, and some leaders blamed invasions for a 15-year-old boy's death from the virus."}, {"id": "7", "subevent": "The Karipuna tribe submitted a complaint in April about non-indigenous clearing inside their reserve; on April 18, an indigenous leader from the Uru-eu-wau-wau reserve was assassinated."}, {"id": "8", "subevent": "In March, Zezico Rodrigues Guajajara was killed by a shotgun-wielding assailant, becoming the fifth Guajajara murdered in five months; Erival Guajajara expressed fear for their lives."}]}

{
  "subevents": [
    {"id": "0", "subevent": "Italy's Economy Minister Roberto Gualtieri said the main business lobby's forecast of a 6% fall in GDP this year is realistic."},
    {"id": "1", "subevent": "On Tuesday, national business association Confindustria said the outbreak would cause a serious recession in 2020."},
    {"id": "2", "subevent": "Gualtieri told Il Fatto Quotidiano that the estimates are realistic and the Italian economy can aim at a vigorous rebound."},
    {"id": "3", "subevent": "The government is scheduled to publish its own estimates in the Document of Economy and Finance (DEF) at the end of April."},
    {"id": "4", "subevent": "Italy's output rose 0.3% last year, and the government expected it to grow 0.6% this year before the coronavirus emerged at the end of February."},
    {"id": "5", "subevent": "At the end of March, two sources told Reuters that the Treasury expected the economy to contract around 3% this year."},
    {"id": "6", "subevent": "Gualtieri said a new stimulus package, set to be approved this month, would be significantly larger than the 25 billion euros passed in March and sufficient for the entire epidemic."},
    {"id": "7", "subevent": "He said the package would include an extension of state-backed guarantees for companies seeking liquidity, unemployment benefits, and support to people on low incomes."},
    {"id": "8", "subevent": "Gualtieri said the use of the European Stability Mechanism (ESM) under current conditions was not an option."},
    {"id": "9", "subevent": "He said Europe needed to coordinate a shared fiscal policy in addition to the European Central Bank's intervention."},
    {"id": "10", "subevent": "He said new solutions are needed to grant parity of conditions and define an adequate shared and responsible response."}
  ]
}

  "subevents": [
    {"id": "0", "subevent": "Malaysia arrested more than 4,000 people for violating lockdown orders."},
    {"id": "1", "subevent": "Malaysia entered a 'harsh mode' of its Movement Control Order to enforce isolation."},
    {"id": "2", "subevent": "Police set up hundreds of roadblocks, conducted inspections, and arrested thousands, including a man who jumped into the Strait of Malacca."},
    {"id": "3", "subevent": "Senior Minister Ismail Sabri Yaakob announced the enforcement shift from soft to stern to harsh mode."},
    {"id": "4", "subevent": "Malaysia reported 4,189 arrests for loitering, with 1,449 charged in court, while the Philippines reported over 20,000 arrests and President Duterte threatened to shoot violators."},
    {"id": "5", "subevent": "Malaysia said its lockdown decreased COVID-19 spread, reporting 3,116 cases and 50 deaths, and Google data showed an 81% decrease in retail and recreation mobility."},
    {"id": "6", "subevent": "Authorities arrested people for allegedly spreading misinformation about the virus, and human rights advocates warned of threats to free expression, with journalists self-censoring."},
    {"id": "7", "subevent": "Digital strategist Jason Kelley of the Electronic Frontier Foundation warned that activists and free expression advocates are in danger when governments curtail speech during crises."},
    {"id": "8", "subevent": "The political crisis following Mahathir Mohamad's failed power consolidation led to the old ruling party returning to power, complicating the pandemic response."},
    {"id": "9", "subevent": "The government announced a $57.3 billion stimulus package called PRIHATIN, including cash aid, loans, deferred taxes, and debt payments."}
  ]
}
